queue.name: dqg_u2off
queue.change_spec: Copy arms/r29 to arms/dqg_u2off and set kernels.py:1174 DQ_U2 = True -> False (verified at that line). k_dkdv, impl.py and _env.py stay byte-identical. Compile gate: k_dkdv stays at 729 VGPR / 70656 B, and k_dqg must match r19h's ISA shape (0 spill). Then arm.sh prod blocked, plus kbench prod blk for the k_dq split. Also take one ATT of k_dqg so the tail-clump loadcnt wait can be compared against U2.
queue.risk: Very low: this configuration already shipped as r19h. No wedge path.
queue.kill_criterion: Prod op time is not at least 0.5% faster than r29 in the same process, or kbench k_dq is not below r29's. If it loses, U2 stays and dqg_tailpf proceeds. If it wins, promote it as the k_dqg base and drop dqg_tailpf.

queue.name: dkdv_lse_late (merges dkdv_lsefence + dkdv_lse_late)
queue.change_spec: Variant a (dkdv_lsefence): insert rocdl.sched_barrier(0) after the b_do/b_q construction loop, before `new = [None]*...` (kernels.py ~L482), so the PHI copy V650<-V693 cannot rise to Vaddr 17140. Variant b, only if variant a's ISA gate fails: issue the hh=0 LSE b32 load after hh=0's last use, with an exp2-anchored z=smin(bits,0) index dependency, so the load lands directly in the carried register. Both variants are bitwise. ISA gate (free): the `s_wait_loadcnt 0x23` + `v_mov v138` pair (CSV:1600-1601, ISA:1611-1612) is gone or moved below the first dK/dV WMMA; no loadcnt wait with a threshold above 0x10 sits between the S/dP WMMAs and phase K; VGPR at most 737; 0 spill. Then arm.sh plus an ATT of k_dkdv.
queue.risk: Low. sched_barrier(0) acts as a boundary, not a clamp (bwd-history closed-axes table), and COPYs may be placed after scheduling, so variant a can yield identical ISA. The free ISA gate catches that. No index change in variant a.
queue.kill_criterion: The ISA gate shows the wait still in front of the copy under both variants (dead at zero card cost). Or prod is below +0.5%, or the ATT phase-H wait is still above 40 cyc/iter.

queue.name: dkdv_ku2_att (re-measure, closed-axis reopen)
queue.change_spec: Copy arms/r29 and set kernels.py:55 KV_U2 = False -> True (verified the flag exists and is off). Compile gate: 0 v_mov_b64 in the loop, VGPR at most 740, 0 spill. Run arm.sh at prod and take an ATT of k_dkdv. Read phase M (the WMMA gaps in the dK/dV tail) and the dscnt wait before the first dK/dV WMMA in both bodies.
queue.risk: Low: the code already exists and is bitwise. The only risk is wasted card time; the prior is negative (c_ku2 +7.3% on B0, lab-kdq REPORT.md:30).
queue.kill_criterion: Prod is not at least +0.5%: record the ATT phase deltas and close it again. Whatever the result, the ATT must show where the removed ~190 cycles went; if they reappear as dscnt or loadcnt wait, mark the M-phase attribution as non-recoverable in single-wave form.

queue.name: dkdv_divfree
queue.change_spec: Remove the two runtime signed divisions ii//G and jj//G in qloop_full, qloop_mask and qloop_full2 (kernels.py:531,539). Preferred form: carry (qi, gh) as loop-state counters, where gh+1 wraps to 0 and increments qi, and the clamped jj reuses the same wrap. Fallback: lgG shift/mask with a host power-of-two assert and the old path kept behind a constexpr flag. Bitwise. ISA gate: no s_mul_hi/s_abs/s_cselect division sequence in .LBB0_11. Today about 27 SALU are at CSV:1374-1400, Vaddr 15628-15732.
queue.risk: Very low. SGPR only. CPU proof needed for the counter wrap and the jj clamp at n-1.
queue.kill_criterion: Loop SALU count is not reduced in the ISA, or prod is below +0.3% when stacked on the rank-2 winner. Promote only as part of a stack if its standalone gain is below the 0.5% threshold.

queue.name: dkdv_trorder (+ qdoburst as variant b)
queue.change_spec: Variant a: fenced 4-region emission of the final DS phase. a_p(kh0) + b_do first, then a_ds(kh0) + b_q with 8 dV WMMAs, then kh1's A operands with the dK kh0 WMMAs, then the rest. Per-slot accumulator order is unchanged, so the result is bitwise. Variant b: also split the hh loop so all 32 Q/dO staging ds_stores are one fenced burst at the top of _body, after nxt=_ldqd (dkdv_qdoburst). ISA gate: the first dK/dV WMMA is preceded by s_wait_dscnt with a threshold of at least 0x10 (today 0x6, CSV:1857); no dscnt 0x0 before the 17th tail WMMA; VGPR at most 760; 0 spill.
queue.risk: Low to medium. Bitwise, no index change. g93 and g94 showed LLVM ignoring order hints, so the free ISA gate decides. Fences can inflate VGPR.
queue.kill_criterion: ISA dscnt threshold before the first dK/dV WMMA is still at most 0x8 (dead for free). Or prod is below +0.5%. Or ATT phase L is still above 120 cyc/iter.

queue.name: dqg_tailpf (merges dqg_earlyclump a/b + dqg_tailpf)
queue.change_spec: Only if dqg_u2off did not win. Keep U2. Issue body 2's K/V prefetch for block ii+2 as one contiguous clump right after the point where the carried set dies. Variant b (preferred for VGPR) splits it per kt, issuing 16 loads once each kt half dies, with a rocdl.sched_barrier(0x78F) VMEM-only fence after each. Same _ldkv(jj*KV_STEP) with the existing clamp, so the output is bitwise. ISA gate: at least ~100 WMMAs between the last clump load and the loop-head s_wait_loadcnt 0x20 (verified today at CSV dispatch_11 line 670, stall 207607/1018 = 204 cyc/trip); VGPR at most 1024; 0 spill; 0 scratch.
queue.risk: Medium on VGPR: k_dqg is at 991/1024 and the fence may stop reuse of registers, which spills. The gate catches it. No wedge path.
queue.kill_criterion: Spill > 0 in both variants. Or the clump lead in the ISA does not grow. Or prod is below +0.5% against the better of r29 and dqg_u2off.

queue.name: mem_soffset_q (xcnt fold; = dqg_earlyclump variant c)
queue.change_spec: In gfrag2/_ldkv (kernels.py ~1230-1275), build K/V loop-load addresses as a loop-invariant per-lane voffset, plus a readfirstlane'd uniform soffset (kv0 row base), plus an immediate dt*64[+32], using rocdl.raw_ptr_buffer_load. The target is the v_or_b32 v90,0xc0,v69 rebuild at CSV dispatch_11:648 and the s_wait_xcnt 0x2 at :647 (verified at 110970/1018 = 109 cyc/trip). The k_dqg descriptors stay fake 1<<30; do not 'fix' them. ISA gate: 0 s_wait_xcnt and at most 2 v_or in the loop; VGPR at most 991.
queue.risk: Medium bounds attention: the address rewrite needs a CPU byte-exact proof over all lanes, dt, kv0 and shapes. No wedge path unless an address goes OOB with a fake descriptor, which is exactly why the proof is mandatory.
queue.kill_criterion: xcnt waits remain in the ISA, the CPU proof fails, or prod is below +0.3% when stacked on the rank-1/6 winner.

queue.name: dqg_dkdv_streams
queue.change_spec: impl.py only: after k_delta, launch k_dqg on a side stream (s2.wait_stream(main)) concurrently with k_dkdv; record_stream on the inputs and dq_o; main.wait_stream(s2) before return. Check that the _launch cache does not bake in the stream. Variant b swaps the launch order. Run the 200-run dk/dv bitwise gate.
queue.risk: Low: no kernel change. With 729/991 VGPR, each SIMD holds one wave of either kernel, so the overlap is only at the tail and ramp boundaries. Possible interference with training-stream semantics in e2e.
queue.kill_criterion: Prod is below +0.4%, or kbench shows the kernels' sum rising (interference) by more than the saved boundary.

queue.name: dkdv_flip
queue.change_spec: As proposed: S = Q*K^T, dP = dO*V^T (swap the WMMA operands at ~L410-415). P and dS become the B operand of dV^T = dO^T*P and dK^T = Q^T*dS directly from the C registers via cvt_pk plus a v8 concat of hh0 and hh1. Delete the P/dS LDS stores and a_p/a_ds tr16. LSE/delta become per-element (8 q rows per lane per hh): budget 16+16 VGPR current plus 32 carried, not +24 as the proposer claimed. Swap the roles in the causal predicate. Write the epilogue directly with row=kv. Host-dispatch r29 when Sq%8 != 0. Validate ≥50 dB and run-to-run bitwise; it cannot be bitwise versus r29, because WMMA operand roles change. Before building, run ablation A1 (noPdS_lds) to price the upper bound.
queue.risk: Medium: new index expressions (vec4 LSE, epilogue, mask) need a CPU proof. VGPR 729 -> ~790. No TDM, no atomics, no wedge path.
queue.kill_criterion: Ablation A1 shows less than 4% k_dkdv gain (then do not build it). Or the compile has spills or VGPR above 850. Or prod is below +1% after stacking on ranks 2-5.

ablations.name: A0_base_att
ablations.spec: The r29 byte copy re-run under the same M8 driver (marker kernel, discard 3, median of 7, PMC GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE/8) plus ATT on CU1, as the reference for every ablation below. No change.
ablations.answers: The same-session noise floor, and the reference per-phase ATT used to compare the ablations.

ablations.name: A1_dkdv_noPdS_lds
ablations.spec: In k_dkdv _body: stop the P/dS round trip. Guard the two P/dS llvm_dialect.store ops with a runtime-false wave-uniform predicate (e.g. qt < 0) so the P/dS VALU is not dead-code eliminated. Replace a_p/a_ds with the already-loaded b_q[0]/b_do[0] fragments, so the 8 tr16 A-operand loads disappear. No index or address change. Output is wrong. ISA check: 0 P/dS ds_store in the loop, 32 tr16 instead of 40, WMMA count unchanged at 64.
ablations.answers: The upper bound of dkdv_flip (and partly of trorder): how many of the 199 dscnt + ~50 switch + ~30 DS-issue cycles are really recoverable once the P/dS LDS dependence is gone. It also rechecks, on reflashed A0, the old P3 finding that deleting LDS ops was not faster.

ablations.name: A2_dkdv_noQdO_vmem
ablations.spec: In qloop_full, carry the previous iteration's Q/dO registers unchanged (nxt Q/dO = pre Q/dO; the LSE/delta loads stay). The 32 buffer_load_b128, the back-edge v_mov_b64 rotation and the WAR v_nops should all vanish; the Q/dO LDS staging and tr16 stay. Output is wrong. ISA check: 4 b32 and 0 b128 loads in the loop, 0 v_mov_b64.
ablations.answers: The light-speed of the Q/dO global path in k_dkdv (phases D, M and part of H/B): the upper bound for dkdv_flip_tdm and the TDM ring. It also shows whether ku2's loss came from something other than the rotation copies.

ablations.name: A3_dkdv_nosm
ablations.spec: In k_dkdv, P = cvt(S) and dS = cvt(dP): skip the scale, -lse, exp2, -delta and multiply. The lse/delta loads stay issued, with their values sunk through a single v_add into one element so they are not removed. Output is wrong. ISA check: 0 v_exp in the loop; WMMA and DS counts unchanged.
ablations.answers: How much of the exposed VALU (phase J 91 plus I/F/G ~78 cyc/iter) is real time, which bounds any fine-grained 3-stage software-pipeline rewrite in the ASM style. Compare with fwd M8, where nosm gave -18.6%.

ablations.name: A4_dqg_noKV_vmem
ablations.spec: In k_dqg's U2 kvloop_full, carry the K/V prefetch set unchanged in both bodies (nxt = pre), so the 64 buffer_load_b128 per trip and the xcnt/loadcnt waits disappear. The K ds_store and tr16 path stays. Output is wrong. ISA check: 0 buffer_load_b128 in the loop, 0 s_wait_xcnt.
ablations.answers: The upper bound of the k_dqg memory path (loadcnt 302 + VMEM issue 214 + xcnt 124 + back-pressure ~60 per trip). It sizes dqg_tailpf, mem_soffset_q and dqg_tdm_kvlds together, and says whether the slow-wave population (wv0/4/8/12) is purely memory.

ablations.name: A5_dkdv_plus_dqwmma
ablations.spec: Add 16 extra WMMAs per k_dkdv iteration, shaped like the fused dQ GEMM (A = the existing dS bf16 fragment or a_ds, B = the resident kf fragments, chained 4 deep from zero). Sink the result once after the loop into an unused accumulator lane via a single add, so it is not dead-code eliminated. No atomics, no new loads. ISA check: 80 WMMA per iteration, VGPR at most 1024, 0 spill.
ablations.answers: What 25% more matrix work costs inside the current 1-wave k_dkdv when the operands are resident. This is stage A of w4_fused_dq without the barrier and w4 confounders, and it separates FUSED5 P1's +30% into the WMMA cost versus the tr16 reload.
